body:
# Independent audit of positive-part weighted fillings

Audited source: `candidate bab3610552c0df1c`, §§1--3.

**PASS for the class closure and pointwise domination statements.** The source correctly leaves the mass comparison unproved.

The full projective map has positive denominator on the compact original body and therefore has convex image. The base Jacobian A^(-n-1), combined with (ell-c)_+^d, gives precisely (1-cA)_+^d A^(-n-d-1). For beta=n+d+1 the inverse root is A/(1-cA)^(d/beta); its displayed second derivative is correct and nonnegative on its convex positive domain. Compactness supplies boundedness. The inverse-power marginal theorem applies since beta>n and leaves exponent beta-n=d+1.

For the positive-part constant subtraction, both displayed derivatives of h/(1-C h^beta)^(1/beta) are correct. The map is convex increasing, and its domain is the convex sublevel {h<C^(-1/beta)}. Boundary zeros are represented by infinite inverse root, so there is no omitted regularity or mass issue.

The one-dimensional lower quadrature charges every full or terminal partial cell [k,k+1] to the integer k. The initial partial cell is the sole exception. The stated upper bound by ell(p_-)^d is valid. A minor sharpening is available directly: because k_0<=p_-, the initial integrand is at most ell(k_0-1)_+^d <= (ell(p_-)-b)_+^d. Thus one can subtract this smaller constant, and if ell(p_-)<=b no subtraction is needed. This does not supply the missing half-mass guarantee.

A later exact certificate, `candidate 037295773376a822`, shows that these class-preserving operations cannot yield a single half-mass minorant on every compatible source-envelope family: such a minorant need not exist at all. Actual deepest/common-Q cap information is therefore necessary for a general application of this route, or the proposed payment mechanism must be weakened.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
